title: Interplay of Excitonic Charge Density Wave and Superconductivity in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
abstract: Motivated by the unique characteristics of the phase diagram of 1T-TiSe2, we investigated the complex interplay of excitonic charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC) on a two-dimensional triangular lattice, each site accommodating two orbitals. In response to various tuning parameters, such as intercalation, pressure, substitution, and gating, these materials exhibit a generic and gradual waning of CDW, followed by the emergence of SC. Intriguingly, the nature of CDW changes from commensurate to incommensurate with the appearance of SC. Setting up a minimal model based on observed excitonic CDW and electron and hole pockets in the Fermi surface, and analyzing it within a simple mean-field framework, we can comprehend some salient experimental features. We also found that the qualitative phase diagram remains insensitive to details of the band structure. These results offer crucial insights into the nature of the interplay between CDW and SC in transition-metal dichalcogenides.
summary: This theoretical work models the competition between excitonic Charge Density Waves and Superconductivity in TMDs using a minimal mean-field Hamiltonian. By analyzing the phase diagram and spectral properties, the authors demonstrate that tuning parameters drive a transition from CDW dominance to SC emergence. The findings provide crucial insights into the intertwined nature of these two correlated electronic orders.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay and competition between excitonic Charge Density Wave (CDW) order and conventional Superconductivity (SC) in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs).
main_result: The phase diagram shows a generic transition where CDW order wanes and SC emerges as tuning parameters change, with the CDW nature evolving from commensurate to incommensurate.
method: The study employs a minimal mean-field model Hamiltonian incorporating both excitonic CDW pairing and intra-band SC attraction, analyzed via self-consistent calculations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled on a two-dimensional triangular lattice using a two-band tight-binding Hamiltonian for the single-particle part. Interactions include excitonic CDW pairing (particle-hole) and conventional SC pairing (intra-band).
key_observables: CDW and SC order parameters ($\chi_q, \Delta$), spectral function $A(k, \omega)$, and the average Density of States (DOS) $N(\omega)$.
important_parameters: Tuning parameters include carrier density ($ho$), and interaction strengths ($W$ for CDW, $U$ for SC).
main_assumptions: The CDW is assumed to have an excitonic origin (inter-band pairing), and SC is assumed to be conventional (intra-band pairing). The model is a minimal toy model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram showing C-CDW to NC-CDW crossover, band structures, and the evolution of the DOS revealing CDW gaps, SC kinks, and their coexistence.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mean-field Hamiltonian, analyzes the ground state energy minimization with respect to the modulation wave vector Q, and then calculates the resulting spectral properties (DOS, FS) across varying carrier densities to map the phase diagram.
why_interesting: The competition between CDW and SC is a canonical problem in strongly correlated electron systems, and the use of excitonic pairing mechanisms provides a rich theoretical framework relevant to understanding unconventional superconductivity.
